# tree_files { #labdata.gitutil.tree_files }

```python
labdata.gitutil.tree_files(repo, rev, path)
```

List every file beneath a directory as of a revision.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Working tree to inspect, on this machine or another.

<code>[**rev**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Revision to read at, typically a commit sha.

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative path of the directory.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`), [int](`int`)\]\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Tuples of ``(path, blob_sha, size)``, sorted by path. Symbolic links are skipped, as they are elsewhere. Sizes are those of the stored blob, so a Git LFS pointer reports the size of the pointer.
